title: Cause and consequence
job: Why things happen and what follows, across a paragraph
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: ONE OF THE TWO CAUSAL ENDINGS MAY HEAD AN ORDER AND THE OTHER MAY NOT. L3-M3's -(eu)nikka can stand in front of an instruction or a suggestion; L1-M9's -aseo cannot, at all. Bappeunikka naeil jeonhwahaseyo is right and bappaseo naeil jeonhwahaseyo is not.

-aseo CARRIES NO TENSE OF ITS OWN. The past sits once, on the main verb: saenggyeoseo ... neujeosseoyo, never saenggyeosseoseo. -(eu)nikka may carry one — gasseonikka — which is the second thing that separates them.

ttaemune LEANS NEGATIVE AND deokbune IS ONLY EVER POSITIVE. English because of covers both, so a learner reaches for ttaemune over a piece of good luck and it reads as blame. Bi ttaemune mot gasseoyo against chingu deokbune jal haesseoyo.

V-ge dwaesseoyo IS THE CONSEQUENCE FRAME: it came about that. It is what Korean reaches for when nobody decided the outcome. Hanguk-e salge dwaesseoyo says circumstances put me there; sal geoyeyo would say I chose it.

THE PASSIVE CLASS IS LEXICAL AND CLOSED. English builds a passive from any transitive verb with be plus a participle. Korean does not: boyeoyo, deullyeoyo and yeollyeoyo are words, and a learner who invents a passive of meokda has invented one. No sentence here writes a by-phrase.

-gi ttaemune IS L3-M3's NOUN FRAME WITH A CLAUSE IN FRONT OF IT. ttaemune does not change; what changes is that the thing before it is a nominalised stem — hagi, gagi, meokgi — bought once by L4-M1 and spent again here.

ABILITY IS NOT REOPENED. L2-M8's mot and L2-M1's -(eu)l su isseoyo are reused as consequences rather than retaught. And nothing counterfactual, which is L4-M3's, no time clause, which is L4-M6's, and no -(seu)pnida, which is L4-M7's.

sentences.cue: There was an accident, so I was very late.

words.note: A crash, a mishap, anything that goes wrong without anyone meaning it to. It is the subject of what happened, so it takes -ga.
Something came into being with no agent behind it. L3-M7's nasseoyo is the symptom that comes out of a body; this is the event that occurs.
Late for a thing, said of a person or of a train. It is a whole verb, not late plus a copula.

sentences.trap: THE PAST SITS ONCE. English marks both halves — there was an accident, so I was late — and Korean marks only the main verb. saenggyeosseoseo is not a form.
sentences.sound: SA-go-ga saeng-GYEO-seo NEO-mu neu-JEO-sseo-yo. Neujeosseoyo is four syllables, with the j soft.

variations.cue: There was an accident, so I was a bit late.
variations.changed: jom softening how late, and the apology with it

variations.cue: Because of the rain I was very late.
variations.changed: the noun-headed cause in place of the ending

mistake.why: -aseo takes no past marker of its own. The tense goes once, on neujeosseoyo, and the reason clause stays saenggyeoseo.

sentences.usage: Explaining yourself as you arrive, before anyone asks.
sentences.mnemonic: One past per sentence, and it goes at the end.

sentences.cue: I am busy right now, so call again tomorrow.

words.note: Once more, from the start. It sits in front of the verb, and it is what makes an instruction sound like a second chance rather than a refusal.

sentences.trap: -(eu)nikka IS THE ONE THAT CAN COMMAND. L3-M3's ending may head an instruction; L1-M9's -aseo may not, and bappaseo jeonhwahaseyo is simply not a sentence. The two are not stylistic neighbours.
sentences.sound: JI-geum ba-PPEU-ni-kka NAE-il DA-si jeon-hwa-HA-se-yo. The double p is held before the ending.

variations.cue: I am busy right now, so let us meet tomorrow.
variations.changed: a suggestion instead of an instruction, which -(eu)nikka also allows

variations.cue: There is no time, so call again.
variations.changed: the reason: no time rather than being busy

mistake.why: -aseo cannot stand in front of a command. A reason that heads an instruction takes -(eu)nikka: bappeunikka.

sentences.usage: Putting someone off politely on the phone, at your desk.

sentences.cue: Because of the accident the door does not open.

words.note: A door or a gate. With the passive it takes -i, because the door is the thing that opens rather than the thing anyone opens.
The door opens, with nobody opening it. One of the three passives this course teaches; the active yeoreoyo would need a person doing it.

sentences.trap: NO ONE IS DOING THIS. English can say the door is not opened and leave the agent hidden; Korean uses a different word. yeollyeoyo has no by-phrase and cannot take one.
sentences.sound: SA-go ttae-MU-ne MU-ni AN yeol-LYEO-yo. The double l is held: yeol-LYEO-yo.

variations.cue: Because of the accident the door would not open.
variations.changed: the past, on the passive verb

variations.cue: Because of the accident I could not get to school.
variations.changed: the consequence: a person who cannot go rather than a door that will not open

mistake.why: deokbune is thanks to, and it is only ever said of good luck. A door stuck shut takes ttaemune.

sentences.usage: Reporting a problem in a building to whoever can fix it.
sentences.mnemonic: The door opens; nobody opens the door.

sentences.cue: Because I am cooking, I have no time.

words.note: L3-M3's word, unchanged. What is new is what may stand in front of it: a nominalised stem — hagi, gagi, meokgi — as well as a plain noun.

sentences.trap: A CLAUSE HAS TO BECOME A NOUN FIRST. ttaemune is a noun frame, so the verb in front of it takes L4-M1's -gi. hae ttaemune and handa ttaemune are both impossible; hagi ttaemune is the shape.
sentences.sound: YO-ri-reul HA-gi ttae-MU-ne. Sigan-i runs together as si-GA-ni.

variations.display: Yori-reul hagi ttaemune jeonhwa-reul mot haesseoyo.
variations.script: 요리를 하기 때문에 전화를 못 했어요.
variations.cue: Because I am cooking, I could not call.
variations.changed: the consequence: a call not made

variations.cue: Because I am making a booking, I have no time.
variations.changed: the clause in front: booking rather than cooking

mistake.why: A bare stem cannot sit in front of ttaemune. The clause is nominalised first, exactly as it is in front of wihaeseo: hagi ttaemune.

sentences.usage: Explaining down the phone why you cannot talk for long.
sentences.mnemonic: -gi turns the clause into the noun ttaemune wants.

sentences.cue: Thanks to a friend I learned Korean well.

words.note: Only ever positive. It names whoever or whatever you owe the good outcome to, and there is no version of it for bad luck.

sentences.trap: ENGLISH because of DOES BOTH JOBS AND KOREAN SPLITS THEM. Choosing ttaemune here would say the friend was the trouble. The choice between the two is not a matter of tone; it says which way the luck went.

variations.cue: Thanks to my teacher I learned Korean well.
variations.changed: who is being thanked

variations.cue: Thanks to a friend it went well.
variations.changed: what went well left unnamed

mistake.why: ttaemune leans negative, so this sounds like blaming the friend for the learning. Good luck takes deokbune.

sentences.usage: Giving somebody credit, out loud, in front of them.

sentences.display: Sori ttaemune jeonhwa-ga jal an deullyeoyo.
sentences.script: 소리 때문에 전화가 잘 안 들려요.
sentences.cue: Because of the noise I cannot hear the phone well.
sentences.literal: noise because-of phone-subj well not is-audible

words.note: Any sound at all, pleasant or not. Whether it is noise is decided by the rest of the sentence rather than by the word.
The sound reaches you; no one is doing the listening. What is heard takes -ga, which is why it is jeonhwa-ga and not jeonhwa-reul.

sentences.trap: THE THING HEARD IS THE SUBJECT. English keeps the hearer in front — I cannot hear the phone — and Korean puts the phone there instead, with -ga. Writing jeonhwa-reul turns it back into active listening.
sentences.sound: SO-ri ttae-MU-ne jeon-HWA-ga JAL AN deul-LYEO-yo. The double l is held: deul-LYEO-yo.

variations.display: Sori ttaemune jeonhwa-ga jal an deullyeosseoyo.
variations.script: 소리 때문에 전화가 잘 안 들렸어요.
variations.cue: Because of the noise I could not hear the phone well.
variations.changed: the past, on the passive verb

variations.cue: Because of the accident the phone cannot be heard.
variations.changed: the cause: an accident rather than the noise

mistake.display: Sori ttaemune jeonhwa-reul jal an deullyeoyo.
mistake.script: 소리 때문에 전화를 잘 안 들려요.
mistake.why: deullyeoyo names the sound arriving, so what arrives is the subject. The particle is -ga, and nobody in the sentence is doing any hearing.

sentences.usage: On a bad line, in a station or a busy street.

sentences.cue: It came about that I live in Korea.

words.note: The -ge shape of salda, waiting for dwaesseoyo behind it. The l of the stem drops in the plain present, which is why that form is sarayo.
The past of L2-M7's dwaeyo, doing a different job: it closes the -ge frame and says circumstances brought the outcome, not a decision.

sentences.trap: THIS IS NOT A PLAN. sal geoyeyo would say you decided to live there. -ge dwaesseoyo says it turned out that way, and Korean reaches for it far more often than English reaches for any equivalent.
sentences.sound: han-GU-ge SAL-ge DWAE-sseo-yo. Dwaesseoyo is two syllables plus the ending: DWAE-sseo-yo.

variations.cue: It came about that I live here.
variations.changed: here rather than a named country

variations.cue: It came about that I do the cooking.
variations.changed: the verb the -ge frame sits on

mistake.why: That says you intend to live there. -ge dwaesseoyo says something outside you settled it, which is what makes it the modest answer.

sentences.usage: Answering how did you end up here? without claiming any credit.
sentences.mnemonic: -ge dwaesseoyo: it turned out that way.

sentences.cue: I turned the light on, so the screen is easy to see.

words.note: The screen is there to be seen. L2-M6's bwayo is a person looking; this is the thing showing, and it takes -i or -ga.

sentences.trap: -aseo AGAIN CARRIES NO TENSE. The turning-on is in the past and the seeing is now, and only the main verb says so. kyeosseoseo is not a form.
sentences.sound: BU-reul KYEO-seo hwa-MYEO-ni JAL bo-YEO-yo. Bul-eul runs together as BU-reul.

variations.cue: I turned the light on, so the screen was easy to see.
variations.changed: the past, on the main verb only

variations.cue: Because of the light the screen is not visible.
variations.changed: the noun-headed cause, and the outcome reversed

mistake.why: bwayo is you doing the looking. boyeoyo says the screen shows up by itself, and what shows up takes -i rather than -eul.

sentences.usage: At a kiosk or a desk, saying whether you can read the screen.

sentences.cue: There is no time, so boil some ramyeon.

words.note: L1-M3's eopseoyo under both causal endings. Only the -(eu)nikka one may head the instruction that follows; the -aseo one may not.

sentences.trap: -(eu)nikka IS THE SPEAKER'S OWN JUSTIFICATION. That is the third thing separating it from -aseo, and it is why it can sound blunt to an elder: it says here is my reason, take it. -aseo just offers a fact.
sentences.sound: si-GA-ni eop-SEU-ni-kka. Eopseunikka has a hard p before the s: eop-SEU-ni-kka.

variations.cue: There was no time, so I boiled some ramyeon.
variations.changed: -aseo with a statement, where -(eu)nikka had an instruction

variations.cue: There is no time, so be quick.
variations.changed: the instruction: hurry rather than cook

mistake.why: -aseo cannot head an instruction, however ordinary the reason is. In front of a command it has to be eopseunikka.

sentences.usage: Telling someone at home what to do about dinner.
sentences.mnemonic: A reason in front of an order is always -nikka.

sentences.display: Geu gyeolgwa hangugeo-reul jal hage dwaesseoyo.
sentences.script: 그 결과 한국어를 잘 하게 됐어요.
sentences.cue: As a result, I came to speak Korean well.
sentences.literal: that result Korean-obj well do-so-that became

words.note: The outcome of what came before. With L2-M10's geu in front and no particle behind it, geu gyeolgwa carries a cause across a sentence break.
The -ge shape of hada, waiting for dwaesseoyo. L3-M4 already owns the bare ge, so this frame costs the course nothing new.

sentences.trap: geu gyeolgwa TAKES NO PARTICLE. It stands at the front of the sentence as a link back to the one before, which is how one cause is carried across a paragraph rather than tied to a single clause.
sentences.sound: GEU gyeol-GWA han-gu-GEO-reul JAL HA-ge DWAE-sseo-yo.

variations.display: Geu gyeolgwa yori-reul jal hage dwaesseoyo.
variations.script: 그 결과 요리를 잘 하게 됐어요.
variations.cue: As a result, I came to cook well.
variations.changed: what came about: cooking rather than Korean

variations.cue: As a result, it came about that I live in Korea.
variations.changed: the outcome: living there

mistake.why: That says you did it well on some occasion. -ge dwaesseoyo says you came to be able to, over time and without deciding to.

sentences.usage: The last sentence of an account of how something turned out.
sentences.mnemonic: geu gyeolgwa carries the cause into the next sentence.

Thanks to a friend I learned Korean well.
